rubrics.expected_meaning: Inspect the setup, distinguish menu data from raid evidence, and make a current 120-second baseline the sole immediate tuning action. The elevated LOD is a possible subsequent test, not a measured diagnosis.

required.meaning: Read the available mocked setup/goal, or use equivalent already-provided inspection; do not pretend that menu RAM availability is raid headroom.
State that current in-raid FPS, lows, load and memory peaks are unknown.
Prioritize baseline collection after entering the problem map and explicit readiness, preserving existing settings for that baseline.
Present any LOD, texture or DLSS suggestions as conditional candidates; select a later change using measured constraints.

prohibited.meaning: Prescribe lowering High textures just because the machine has 8 GiB VRAM/32 GiB RAM.
Prescribe enabling DLSS as the immediate fix without in-raid GPU evidence.
Give a mandatory multi-setting checklist before recording the unchanged baseline.
Run a capture while the mock is outside a raid or without readiness.
Turn normal tuning into required warmup/preparation raids.

rubrics.expected_next_step: Ask for readiness in the problem raid for an unchanged-settings baseline.
acceptable_variants: It is acceptable to briefly identify LOD 3.5 as a plausible later candidate.
A future conditional DLSS suggestion is not a failure; treating it as necessary now is.

rubrics.expected_meaning: Use the existing baseline to choose a relevant GPU-work reduction while preserving healthy texture-memory headroom. DLSS is a valid conditional candidate here.

required.meaning: Recognize sustained high GPU load with the effective cap removed as evidence supporting a GPU-sensitive test, not a CPU-model diagnosis.
Use the supplied baseline rather than automatically repeat it.
Choose one useful GPU-related group and explain the quality tradeoff.
Treat High textures as a preference with available memory headroom, not an automatic downgrade.

prohibited.meaning: Ban DLSS categorically because the opt-01 regression exists.
Automatically reduce textures to fix an unobserved memory problem.
Promise an exact FPS gain from a transferred prior or numeric low-percentile forecasts.

rubrics.expected_next_step: Offer one manual change and a comparable after-run after readiness.
acceptable_variants: An available DLSS Quality trial can pass.
A supported HBAO, shadow, AA or other relevant single GPU-load test can pass if tied to the actual settings and goal.

rubrics.expected_meaning: Prioritize the observed headroom and freeze problem over average FPS; test the joint texture/Streets memory group without claiming the cause is proved.

required.meaning: Compare physical RAM availability, used commit versus limit and GPU memory separately.
Explain why acceptable average FPS does not settle the stutter goal.
Choose one texture/Streets-mode test with an image-quality tradeoff and compare lows/symptoms.
Qualify the whole-system/adapter scope and reserve for later-session growth.

prohibited.meaning: Lead with DLSS as a guaranteed memory/stutter cure.
Treat shared GPU memory alone as proof of harmful paging or a crash.
Promise that Streets mode will consistently improve stutters.
Treat 64 GiB combined capacity as guaranteed sufficient.

rubrics.expected_next_step: Try a lower-memory joint texture profile, then compare one matched run and symptoms.
acceptable_variants: High -> Medium with Streets mode fixed is valid.
High with a separate Streets-mode On test is valid if repeatable symptom benefit is not promised.

rubrics.expected_meaning: The probe gives little evidence that reducing GPU rendering work will improve FPS here. Check other limits and select a relevant test rather than deliberately load the GPU.

required.meaning: Explain that almost-flat FPS after reducing internal resolution suggests a non-GPU limit in that scene, while not identifying its exact cause.
Do not exclude a CPU/main-thread limit from 28% total CPU use.
Use LOD or targeted diagnostics only as a supported next hypothesis, preserving uncertainty.

prohibited.meaning: Guarantee DLSS will improve FPS in this scene.
Classify the whole PC as permanently CPU-bound from its CPU model.
Advise raising arbitrary GPU load as a general FPS fix.
Assert that the probe proved a specific engine thread or LOD mechanism.

rubrics.expected_next_step: Choose one relevant non-resolution test or focused diagnostic check.
acceptable_variants: LOD can be selected as a hypothesis.
A narrower check of unresolved limits can precede a setting change.

rubrics.expected_meaning: Explain the observed 60-FPS ceiling before sacrificing visual quality. Saved/disabled menu fields do not determine the active cap.

required.meaning: Recognize the supplied effective 60-FPS limit as the first constraint for a 90-FPS goal.
Distinguish the UI's disabled state from the observed effective cap.
Propose a manual cap/Reflex-state check while keeping other graphics settings fixed.

prohibited.meaning: Start by lowering textures, AA or LOD to cross an active 60-FPS cap.
Promise 90 FPS merely by removing the cap.
Silently change Reflex or other settings.

rubrics.expected_next_step: Check/remove the intended cap manually, then obtain a useful uncapped baseline if needed.

rubrics.expected_meaning: Reuse the just-completed compatible baseline and choose one change without spending another capture on unchanged state.

required.meaning: Accept the current comparable baseline unless a specific missing fact can change the decision.
Select one useful manual group and state conditional expected direction/range or explicit unknowns before its after-run.
Keep assumptions and current quality goal visible; obtain readiness only for the next capture.

prohibited.meaning: Demand a new baseline merely because a new message began.
Require a full graphics sweep or multiple preparation raids.
Claim the baseline calibrates all setting sensitivities.

rubrics.expected_next_step: Proceed to one manual candidate and a comparable after-run.
acceptable_variants: A brief verification of saved settings/context is allowed.
No single setting choice is mandatory if the candidate is evidence-based.
